column1: # Digium interface cards, by peripheral bus device identifier.
# THIS FILE IS THE ONE PLACE THESE IDENTIFIERS ARE WRITTEN DOWN. The control
# plane reads it to name a detected card, and the pre-flight script reads it to
# tell an installer what is in the machine before anything is installed. There
# were two tables before this file, one in each of those places, and they
# disagreed with each other on ten of the eleven identifiers they shared.
# The disagreement was not cosmetic. Device zero two zero five was named as a
# four port analogue card by one table and as a dual span digital card by the
# other. An operator installing a digital card was told they had an analogue
# one; the wizard would then have offered them the wrong questions, and the
# wrong driver module would have been named in the diagnosis when it did not
# come up.
# PROVENANCE. Every row below was read out of the driver source that this
# product compiles into its own image, at version:
#     DAHDI Linux v3.4.0-rc1-20-gd1c842a
# specifically the PCI device tables in drivers/dahdi/*/base.c and
# drivers/dahdi/*-base.c. They were extracted mechanically rather than
# transcribed, because transcribing thirty-five hexadecimal identifiers by hand
# is how the two tables this file replaces came to be wrong. Nothing here is
# from memory or from a vendor page.
# WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. That an identifier is listed here means the driver
# claims it. It does not mean this product has been run against that card: no
# physical Digium card has been in a machine running this appliance. See
# docs/hardware-compatibility.md, where every such row is marked UNVERIFIED.
# Four identifiers that the two previous tables carried are absent here --
# eight zero zero two, eight zero zero five, eight zero zero six, and zero
# eight zero zero. No driver in this source claims them. They were invented,
# and a card that never existed cannot be diagnosed.
# Where the driver distinguishes generations of the same card by the subsystem
# identifier, the generation is left off the model name: the appliance reads
# only the vendor and device from the bus, so it cannot tell a fourth
# generation card from a third and must not pretend to.
# Columns, separated by tabs:
#   device
